title: Fair Representation Learning: An Alternative to Mutual Information

problem.claim: Fair representation learning aims to reduce bias in data-oriented decision making by learning representations independent of sensitive attributes.

gap.claim: Existing approaches primarily minimize mutual information, but direct computation is intractable and commonly used upper bounds may remain intractable or harm representation utility.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces distance covariance as a dependence measure for fair representation learning.
It converts distance covariance into a tractable penalty for categorical sensitive attributes without contradicting the utility desideratum.
It proposes FairDisCo, a variational method for learning fair representations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments show FairDisCo outperforms existing competitors for fair representation learning.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fair representation learning is important for reducing bias and protecting minority subgroups.
Existing work commonly approximates independence by minimizing mutual information.
Mutual-information computation and some upper bounds are intractable, while other bounds may conflict with representation utility.
The paper uses distance covariance, derives a tractable penalty for categorical sensitive attributes, and proposes FairDisCo.
Experiments are reported to show that FairDisCo outperforms existing competitors.

source_observation.claim: A dependence measure can be selected and reformulated to exploit the categorical structure of sensitive attributes.

interpretation.claim: Matching the objective to known data structure may improve tractability while preserving a utility constraint.

application.claim: When designing fairness objectives, investigate structured dependence measures that yield computable penalties for the attribute types present in the data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this reformulation generalizes beyond the stated categorical-sensitive-attribute setting.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, and experimental conditions are not specified.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results or details of the variational objective.
Computational complexity and representation utility are not independently verified.
